title: Enterprise Assurance Routing Conductor: intelligent triage and SLA routing for security & compliance asks
creator: Aisha Monroe
description:
Problem:
Many enterprise security and compliance requests (SOC2 evidence bundles, vendor questionnaires, DPAs, data residency clarifications, HIPAA scoping) arrive via multiple channels (sales, support, account teams). Current triage is manual, inconsistent, and takes multiple touchpoints across Legal, Security, and Engineering, causing slow SLA times and repeat work.

Goal:
Design and ship the "Routing Conductor": an intelligent intake and routing layer that classifies incoming enterprise compliance asks, synthesizes required artifacts and the minimal remediation path, and routes to a prioritized lane with clear SLA, required owners, and templated responses. The Conductor should reduce human handoffs, shorten time-to-first-response, and increase automated response coverage while surfacing high-risk items for manual review.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Median time-to-first-response for enterprise compliance asks reduced from ~48h to <= 8h.
- Percent of incoming vendor questionnaires with a first-pass automated answer draft >= 60%.
- Reduction in Legal/Sec engineering manual triage cycles by 40%.
- % of asks correctly routed to dedicated vs hosted vs private lanes within SLA >= 95% measured on sample audits.

Scope:
- Intake channels: shared inbox, internal Support->Compliance tag, Sales handoff UI, and API ingestion for high-volume customers.
- Classifiers: risk score (low/medium/high), data residency sensitivity, hosting-mode sensitivity (hosted/dedicated/private), regulatory domain (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA).
- Routing lanes: fast-path automated bundle (templates + canned evidence), standard Legal review lane, Dedicated deployment ops lane, Private deployment onboarding lane.
- Output: routed ticket with lane, SLA target, required artifact checklist, suggested owner(s), suggested canned response draft, and confidence score.

Design proposals (high level):
1) Hybrid rule + model classifier: deterministic business rules (e.g., if questionnaire includes 'PHI' -> HIPAA path) then LLM-assisted signal enrichment to extract entity mentions, control IDs, and evidence keys.
2) Evidence manifest: normalized schema listing required artifacts (SOC2 reports, DPIA, encryption-at-rest confirmation, architecture diagram) and links to canonical docs in Drive/Confluence.
3) SLA lanes and escalation matrix: define explicit SLOs by lane and account tier (P0 enterprise: 8h first response, P1: 24h, P2: 72h).
4) Auto-draft engine: uses curated templates + knowledge-base to produce a first-draft response and a checklist for the account team to review.
5) Observability: per-ticket audit trail, time-in-lane metrics, accuracy of auto-drafts vs final responses, and a small sample human audit workflow to regularly calibrate classifiers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest sample of 100 historical enterprise asks; the Conductor correctly classifies routing lane and produces required evidence manifest for >= 90% (manual verification).
- Auto-draft engine produces an answer draft for at least 60% of questionnaires with confidence >= 0.7.
- Routing UI surfaces lane, SLA, checklist, and suggested owner in the first screen and allows reassignment and notes.
- Audit log includes classifier signals, extracted evidence keys, and link to original artifact.

Implementation plan (MVP):
- Week 1-2: Data collection and annotation of historical requests (collab: Legal, Security, Solutions Eng).
- Week 3: Build deterministic rule set for high-risk signals (PHI, data residency, contractual clauses).
- Week 4: Prototype LLM enrichment pipeline for entity/control extraction and evidence manifest generation.
- Week 5: Integrate with Linear intake endpoint and Console ticketing view; wire up lane definitions and SLAs.
- Week 6: Pilot with 3 enterprise accounts and Sales/ASM intake; collect feedback and calibrate.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Over-automation risk: mis-routed high-risk asks must never be auto-closed. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, always require manual approval for high-risk lane.
- Data privacy: classifier enrichment must not leak customer PII to third-party services. Mitigation: enrichment runs in private VPC and uses local models where possible; redact PHI before transient logging.
- Operational overhead: building a canonical evidence store requires Legal and Docs effort. Mitigation: start with prioritized controls and expand iteratively.

Open questions for kickoff:
- Which channels should be prioritized for MVP ingestion (Sales only vs all channels)?
- What is the minimum evidence manifest schema needed to satisfy SOC2/DPA/HIPAA triage?
- Do we permit auto-drafts to be sent directly from the Conductor or only suggested to an assigned reviewer?
